guarantees.title: The artifact contract cannot drift
guarantees.claim: 10 dataclasses in artifacts.py are mirrored by TypeScript interfaces in web/lib/types.ts. Nothing in either toolchain notices when they diverge: Python keeps writing, TypeScript keeps compiling, and the site renders undefined for a field somebody renamed.
guarantees.how: tests/test_artifacts.py parses types.ts and fails on any field present on one side and not the other.

guarantees.title: The live agent runs the same defenses as the corpus
guarantees.claim: The /agent demo needs a server, and that server is Node — so the injection classifier, tool scoping and HITL policy exist in TypeScript as well as Python. Two implementations of one security control is how a demo drifts into looking right while being wrong.
guarantees.how: Every scoreable span of every spliced document is scored by both, and compared on score, on the reasons that fired, and on the redacted document byte for byte.

guarantees.title: The in-browser detector is the trained model
guarantees.claim: The site walks the 400-tree ensemble in JavaScript so a visitor does not download 3.2MB of inference runtime to see a score. That is only a good trade if the answer is unchanged.
guarantees.how: Every row the demo can display is scored through the exported ONNX graph and through the JavaScript walker, and the two are diffed.

guarantees.title: Fixture data announces itself
guarantees.claim: Every artifact carries a placeholder flag, a git sha and a timestamp. While any artifact on the page is a seeded fixture, a banner sits above the header on every route and names the exact files — so no figure on this site can quietly be invented.
guarantees.how: The writers set the flag; the site reads it and refuses to hide it.
